title: Representative presentation of a commutative ringed tensor square
statement:
Fix a universe of module sheaves and small sites. A corner presentation consists of a small site, a sheaf of commutative rings R, its unbounded derived category D(R), and a bifunctor T:D(R)×D(R)→D(R) with its natural identification with total tensor on pairs of K-flat complexes with flat terms, as in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. An edge presentation from the R-corner to the S-corner (the direction of inverse image) consists of a geometric inverse image I with its right adjoint, its algebraic lift [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image], a ring map c:I(R)→S, the additive module pullback P(M)=S⊗_{I(R)}I(M) on objects and morphisms, its module right adjoint, its total left derived functor L with its derived comparison, and a right adjoint U of L with an adjunction L⊣U. Right adjoints are models of the ordinary and derived module direct images; their unique adjunction-compatible identifications allow any such models. Retain the canonical ordinary tensor comparison, including its scalar-insertion maps q and generalized pure-tensor equation, from [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. For corners Y,X,Y',X' and edges f:Y→X, g:Y→Y', h:X→X', k:Y'→X' in this inverse-image direction, a ringed square presentation consists of a natural isomorphism α:I_k I_g≅I_h I_f on sheaves of sets and its linear module comparison a:P_k P_g≅P_h P_f, characterized by
$$a_M\,q_k(P_gM)\,I_k(q_g(M))=q_h(P_fM)\,I_h(q_f(M))\,α_{|M|}.$$
Here q_u:I_u|M|→|P_uM| is specifically insertion of 1 in extension of scalars, and all terms use the algebraic-lift underlying-sheaf identifications. Linearity and this generator equation express compatibility with the structural ring maps, and fix the module comparison uniquely. There is no cartesianness or flatness condition, and no derived-square tensor coherence is included as data. The edge derived tensor comparison is the unique representative-normalized comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback].
